summary: Target-level plan for the cyclotomic main conjectures of modular forms. L0 fixes the modular Iwasawa datum (geometric normalisation, the Skinner–Urban twist T = T_f(det ρ_f^{-1}), Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ(G_∞)), constructs the ordinary Selmer dual, the ordinary p-adic L-function with canonical periods, Kato's Iwasawa cohomology and fundamental line and the LLZ signed Selmer groups, states the three main conjectures as propositions, and proves the structure theorem and the two comparisons (Kato 17.13; LLZ Corollary 6.6). L1 proves the Skinner–Urban form (requested by HE.0 and BSD.0), the Fouquet–Wan 1.6 form along FW §4.8, the Selmer form and Skinner's multiplicative-reduction theorem; L2–L4 import Fouquet–Wan's pointwise and family endpoints and the BCS theorems from AutomorphicCongruences (RS-11 narrowings) and prove the convention, lattice/period and signed comparisons; L5 gives Euler-factor, coefficient and μ/λ invariance, the rank-zero converse, the ℒ-invariant, the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum conjecture, trivial zeros, Schneider's implication and worked examples (11a1 at 7, 14a1 at 13 and 5, and η⁴(z)η⁴(5z) at 7 conditional on the recorded ramification input); L6 is the interface to the separately proved anticyclotomic, Eisenstein, supersingular and multiplicative branches.

nodes.title: The modular Iwasawa datum
nodes.statement: A modular Iwasawa datum D = (f, p, L, T_f) consists of: an odd prime p with fixed embeddings ι_∞ : Q̄ → C and ι_p : Q̄ → Q̄_p; a newform f ∈ S_k(Γ_1(N), ε) of weight k ≥ 2; a finite extension L/Q_p containing ι_p(Q(f)), with ring of integers O, uniformiser ϖ and residue field F; the two-dimensional L-representation ρ_f : G_Q → Aut_L(V_f) of Deligne in geometric normalisation, so that for ℓ ∤ Np the geometric Frobenius has characteristic polynomial X² − a_ℓ(f)X + ε(ℓ)ℓ^{k−1} and L(V_f, s) = L(f, s); and a G_Q-stable O-lattice T_f ⊂ V_f. Put T := T_f(det ρ_f^{-1}), V := T[1/p], A := V/T (so that T ≅ T_pE when f = f_E has weight two and trivial character), Γ := Gal(Q_∞/Q) for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension Q_∞, G_∞ := Gal(Q(μ_{p^∞})/Q) ≅ Δ × Γ with Δ ≅ (Z/p)^×, Λ := O[[Γ]], Λ(G_∞) := O[[G_∞]], γ ∈ Γ the generator corresponding to 1 + p under the cyclotomic character κ, and ι : Λ → Λ the involution induced by g ↦ g^{-1}. The residual representation ρ̄ is the reduction of T_f modulo ϖ; its semisimplification does not depend on T_f. The datum is good ordinary when p ∤ N and a_p(f) ∈ O^×; then V_f has a unique G_{Q_p}-stable line V_f^+ on which inertia acts trivially, and T^+ := (T_f ∩ V_f^+)(det ρ_f^{-1}). The ordinary datum satisfies (dist) when the two characters of G_{Q_p} on ρ̄^{ss} restricted to G_{Q_p} are distinct, and (irred) when ρ̄ is irreducible. For the multiplicative branch only, also allow a weight-two p-new form of level N₀p, p ∤ N₀, with a_p = ±1: use its unramified cohomological subline and the same saturated determinant twist (Skinner 2016 §2.1, pp.5–6). In this roadmap ordinary includes this specified semistable case; good ordinary always requires p ∤ N.
hypotheses: p odd; f a newform; L contains the Hecke field and, for an ordinary datum, the roots of X² − a_p X + ε(p)p^{k−1}

geometric normalisation of ρ_f, as in Skinner–Urban; Kato's V_{F_λ}(f) is related to it by the dictionary of KatoEulerSystems:L2/hecke-dual-twist-dictionary, and Fouquet–Wan's cohomological ρ_f (det = χ_cyc^{1−k} for trivial ε) by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-convention-dictionary
proofSteps: Take ρ_f and its integral lattices from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/ordinary-refinement-and-saturated-lattice (ordinary case) and R19.5/good-nonordinary-crystalline-wach-realisation (crystalline nonordinary case); the line V_f^+ and saturation T_f ∩ V_f^+ are the ordinary refinement supplied there (Skinner–Urban §1.1, p.2).

The twist by det ρ_f^{-1} is the one Skinner–Urban use to define their Selmer group (§1.1, p.2); for f = f_E the identification T ≅ T_pE comes from EllipticCurveModularity:R29.4/tate-module-comparison and the Weil pairing.
Λ, Λ(G_∞), the involution and the identification Λ ≅ O[[X]], γ ↦ 1 + X, are those of the completed group rings of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1.
acceptance: For f = f_E attached to 11a1 (weight 2, N = 11, ε = 1) and p = 7: a_7 = −2 ∈ Z_7^×, so the datum is ordinary; the unit root α of X² + 2X + 7 is congruent to −2 mod 7.
Changing T_f to ϖT_f gives the same T up to the isomorphism multiplication by ϖ; changing it to a non-homothetic lattice changes T but not ρ̄^{ss}.

nodes.title: The ordinary Selmer group over Q_∞ and its dual
nodes.statement: For an ordinary modular Iwasawa datum and a finite set Σ of primes not containing p, the Σ-imprimitive ordinary Selmer group is Sel^Σ(Q_∞, A) := the subgroup of H¹(Q_∞, A) of classes that are unramified at every finite place of Q_∞ not above p or Σ and whose restriction to the decomposition group at the unique place above p maps to zero in H¹(Q_{∞,p}, (T/T^+) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p); Sel(Q_∞, A) is the case Σ = ∅. Its Pontryagin dual X^Σ := Hom_cont(Sel^Σ(Q_∞, A), Q_p/Z_p) is a finitely generated Λ-module, with Λ acting on the dual through ι (the contragredient action). The same construction over Q(μ_{p^∞}) gives a Λ(G_∞)-module X^Σ(G_∞) whose η-components, for η ∈ Δ^∨, are obtained by the explicit discrete-coefficient twist A ⊗ η over Q_∞, with the local conditions twisted as well; a modular-form identification additionally uses the Hecke dual/twist dictionary.
hypotheses: good ordinary datum, or the explicitly specified weight-two multiplicative datum
Σ finite, p ∉ Σ; the conditions at Σ are relaxed (no condition)
finite generation over Λ is unconditional; torsion is a theorem under hypotheses (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-structure), never part of the definition
proofSteps: Instantiate the Greenberg local condition SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/greenberg-condition at p with F^+ = T^+ and the unramified condition SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/unramified-condition away from pΣ, over the cyclotomic tower; the global group is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/galois-selmer-group in its discrete form and the dual is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/pontryagin-dual.

Skinner–Urban define the condition at p as vanishing in H¹(Q_{∞,p}, (T/T^+) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) (§1.1, p.2). Since Q_{∞,p}/Q_p is totally ramified, the kernel of H¹(Q_{∞,p}, A^-) → H¹(I, A^-) is A^-/(φ − 1)A^-, which is zero whenever the unramified Frobenius eigenvalue on A^- := (T/T^+) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p is not 1; so the strict and inertial forms agree unless α = 1, and the strict form is the one used.

Finite generation of X^Σ follows from that of H¹(Q_Σ'/Q_∞, A)^∨ over Λ (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-finiteness-euler) by Nakayama over the compact local ring Λ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5).

Relaxing Σ: X^Σ surjects onto X with kernel the dual of ⊕_{ℓ∈Σ} H¹(Q_{∞,ℓ}, A) (Skinner–Urban Proposition 3.2.18, p.27) when X is torsion and T* has no G_Q-fixed vectors. Here Σ ∪ {p} contains the ramification set.

nodes.title: Structure of the ordinary Selmer dual
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary modular Iwasawa datum with trivial character. (1) X^Σ is finitely generated over Λ. (2) If p ∤ N, then X is Λ-torsion (Kato 17.4(1)); for f = f_E with E/Q non-CM and good ordinary or multiplicative at p, Z_∞ = Sel(E/Q_∞)^∨ is torsion. (3) If X^Σ is torsion, ρ̄ is irreducible, and Greenberg's local hypotheses hold (for the quoted Rubin elliptic case: E non-CM and good ordinary at p and p ∤ ∏_{q|N} #E(Q_q)_tors), then X^Σ has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule. (4) Under (3), char_Λ(X^Σ) = Fitt_Λ(X^Σ) is principal, and char_Λ(X^Σ) does not depend on the lattice T_f.
hypotheses: ordinary datum, trivial character
(2) uses p ∤ N for the non-elliptic case
(3) needs X^Σ torsion and the local hypotheses of Greenberg's theorem; for Σ-imprimitive X^Σ Skinner–Urban Lemma 3.2.17(i) gives the absence of pseudo-null submodules of the local terms
(4) the Fitting comparison is over Λ ≅ O[[X]] for modules with no nonzero finite submodule and projective dimension one

nodes.title: The ordinary p-adic L-function with canonical periods
nodes.statement: For an ordinary datum with trivial character and p ∤ N, let α be the unit root of X² − a_p X + p^{k−1} and Ω_f^± the canonical periods of f (generators of the saturated integral period lattices, defined up to O^× ∩ Q(f)). The ordinary p-adic L-function L_f ∈ Λ is the unique element such that for every finite-order character φ of Γ with φ(γ) = ζ a primitive p^{t−1}-th root of unity and every integer 0 ≤ m ≤ k − 2, φκ^m(L_f) = e(φκ^m)·p^{t'(m+1)} m! L(f, χ_φ^{-1}ω^{-m}, m+1) / ((−2πi)^{m+1} G(χ_φ^{-1}ω^{-m}) Ω_f^{sgn((−1)^m)}), with e the interpolation factor built from α, as in Skinner–Urban §1.1 with the correction in Skinner 2016, §2.4, footnote 6 (p.14). For a finite set Σ of primes not containing p, L_f^Σ := L_f · ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ), where P_{T,ℓ} is Skinner–Urban's Euler polynomial of T at ℓ (the polynomial of their Lemma 3.2.17(ii), so that the same factor appears on the Selmer side) and γ_ℓ ∈ Γ is the image of Frob_ℓ. L_f lies in Λ (not only Λ[1/p]) because the canonical periods are integral normalisations. Here χ_φ is the primitive p-power-order Dirichlet character with χ_φ(1+p) = ζ⁻¹, p^{t′} is the conductor of ω^mχ_φ, κ is the cyclotomic character with κ(γ)=1+p, and G is the Gauss sum. For the weight-two multiplicative branch replace α by a_p = ±1 and use the multiplicative interpolation factor of Skinner §2.4; the trivial value has one factor 1−α⁻¹. The integral normalization is Skinner–Urban’s canonical normalization. Its identification with a particular saturated modular-symbol lattice and Kato good dual pair must retain any period scalar; the integral comparison is the explicit gap below. Write P_f^± := −2πi Ω_f^± for the corresponding differential/modular-symbol periods. If the modular-symbol supplier calls its periods Ω, first translate that notation to P_f; do not substitute P_f for the cohomological Ω_f in this formula.
hypotheses: ordinary, p ∤ N, trivial character
canonical periods as supplied by ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/integral-period-lattices; a different choice changes L_f by an element of O^×
the measure is the ordinary branch of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/ordinary-integral-measure restricted to the cyclotomic Z_p-direction through the twist by ω^{-m}
The coefficient lattice is the one compatible with the specified canonical normalization. If a supplier measure uses a different lattice, carry its scalar rather than infer it is an O-unit.
proofSteps: Take the ordinary integral measure μ_{f,α} on Z_p^× of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/ordinary-integral-measure with the period lattice normalisation of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/integral-period-lattices. Translate the supplier’s differential period P_f to Ω_f=P_f/(−2πi) before writing the interpolation formula.
Push it to Γ through the projection Z_p^× → 1 + pZ_p ≅ Γ after the appropriate Teichmüller twist; interpolation and uniqueness are ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/interpolation-and-uniqueness.
The Σ-depleted function is the primitive/imprimitive comparison ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L4/primitive-imprimitive-level-change.
acceptance: In weight two, changing Ω_f^+ by a unit u ∈ O^× multiplies L_f by u^{-1} and leaves the ideal (L_f) unchanged; changing it by ϖ changes (L_f) by ϖ^{-1}, so the integral equality of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-main-conjecture is sensitive to the period normalisation.

nodes.title: The Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for an ordinary form
nodes.statement: For an ordinary datum D with trivial character and p ∤ N, and a finite set Σ of primes not containing p, IMC^Σ(D) is the proposition: X^Σ is a torsion Λ-module and char_Λ(X^Σ) = (L_f^Σ) as ideals of Λ. The rational form IMC^Σ_Q(D) asserts the same equality in Λ[1/p] = Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p. For f = f_E it is Mazur's main conjecture in the normalisation of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/mazur-main-conjecture. The proposition is a statement, not an axiom: conditional consequences explicitly list it as an assumption (in particular Schneider’s leading-term implication).
hypotheses: ordinary datum, trivial character, p ∤ N

proofSteps: Form X^Σ (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-dual) and L_f^Σ (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/canonical-ordinary-padic-l-function).
Use the characteristic ideal of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 §4.6; the rational form compares ideals after extension of scalars to Λ[1/p].

The integral statement is meaningful only after the period normalisation is fixed; Skinner–Urban §1.1 (p.2) note the characteristic ideal depends on T_f only through its ϖ-adic valuation, and not at all when ρ̄ is irreducible.
acceptance: IMC^Σ(D) for one Σ is equivalent to IMC^{Σ'}(D) for every Σ' (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/euler-factor-change).
IMC(D) implies IMC_Q(D); the converse holds when μ(X) = μ(L_f) (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/mu-lambda-comparison).

nodes.title: Iwasawa cohomology, the zeta element and the fundamental line
nodes.statement: For a modular Iwasawa datum with the lattice T_K in Kato's normalisation (the dictionary of KatoEulerSystems:L2/hecke-dual-twist-dictionary), put H^i(T_K) := lim_n H^i_et(Z[ζ_{p^n}, 1/p], j_*T_K) for i = 1, 2, Λ(G_∞)-modules, and RΓ_Iw(T_K) the corresponding perfect complex of Λ(G_∞)-modules with j_* conditions (extension by zero is not used; ramified primes keep the j_* condition). The Iwasawa fundamental line is the invertible Λ(G_∞)-module Δ_Iw(T_K) := Det^{-1}_{Λ(G_∞)} RΓ_Iw(T_K) ⊗ Det^{-1}_{Λ(G_∞)} (T_K ⊗ Λ(G_∞))(−1)^+, and Kato's zeta element z_f ∈ H¹(T_K) ⊗ Q (KatoEulerSystems:L2/integral-zeta-submodule-and-finite-index, the Λ-module Z(f, T_K) generated by Kato's zeta elements) defines, through the zeta morphism T_K(−1)^+ → H¹, a trivialisation triv_z : Δ_Iw(T_K) ⊗ Frac → Q(Λ(G_∞)). The same construction over Q_∞ (Λ in place of Λ(G_∞)) gives Δ_Iw over Λ = O[[Γ]], the form used by Fouquet–Wan. Here Q(Λ(G_∞)) denotes the total quotient ring, a product of fraction fields of the η-components, not a field. The primitive j_* complex is used only with its perfectness and local comparison hypotheses. For general family coefficients use Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.18’s modified local factors, not an unconditional j_* complex.
hypotheses: p odd
H¹(T_K) torsion-free of Λ-rank one and H²(T_K) torsion (Kato Theorem 12.4) are theorems, used to identify the determinant with an invertible fractional ideal
the {p}-partial complex over Z[1/p] is the one in Kato's Conjecture 12.10; the Σ-partial complex over Z[1/Σ] is used in families and changes Δ by Euler factors
The j_* / continuous comparison is only the supported comparison in the indicated degrees; do not infer a complex equivalence from the H¹ edge sequence alone.
proofSteps: Iwasawa cohomology and its finiteness are SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-cohomology and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-finiteness-euler; the étale/continuous comparison is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/etale-iwasawa-comparison.
The determinant functor and the height-one divisor of an acyclic-after-Frac perfect complex are PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5 §5.1 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/selmer-determinant.

The zeta morphism is Kato's (KatoEulerSystems:L2/rational-kato-zeta-morphism and, over deformation rings, KatoEulerSystems:L2/nakamura-twisted-zeta-morphism); Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.3 and Theorem 3.4 record it as the {p}-partial zeta morphism z(f)_Iw.

nodes.title: Zeta basis versus characteristic ideals
nodes.statement: Let λ be an Iwasawa-suitable classical specialisation in the sense of Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.12 (in particular ρ̄ satisfies their Assumption 2.1 and there is ℓ ∥ N, ℓ ≠ p, with dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1). Then H¹(T_λ,Iw) is free of rank one over O_Iw, the integral cone C of z(λ)_Iw has cohomology H¹/z in degree one and H² in degree two, while C ⊗ Frac(O_Iw) is acyclic (V_λ,Iw in Lemma 3.13 already denotes fraction-field coefficients), and consequently: z(λ)_Iw is a basis of Δ_Iw(T_λ) iff char H²(T_λ,Iw) = char(H¹(T_λ,Iw)/O_Iw·z(λ)_Iw). Moreover Kato's divisibility char(H¹/z) ⊂ char(H²) holds integrally for such λ.

nodes.title: Kato's main conjecture versus the ordinary main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary datum with trivial character, p ∤ N, p odd, with α the unit root, and let L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f) be Kato's p-adic zeta function for a good pair (ω, γ) for the dual lattice. For every height-one prime 𝔭 of Λ not containing p there is an exact sequence of Λ_𝔭-modules 0 → (H¹/Z)_𝔭 → (H¹_loc/H¹_loc')_𝔭/(image of Z) → X_𝔭 → H²_𝔭 → 0 (Kato (17.13.1) localised), whose middle term has length ord_𝔭(L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f)) by the Coleman map; hence length(X_𝔭) = ord_𝔭(L_{p-adic}) iff length(H²_𝔭) = length((H¹/Z)_𝔭). If in addition ρ̄ has a unipotent element with free rank-one coinvariants (or Kato's (12.5.2)) and p ≠ 2, the same holds at 𝔭 = (ϖ). Consequently KMC(T_K), on the η-component matched with D by Kato's twist T ↦ T(k) in (17.13.1), is equivalent to IMC(D), and KMC_Q to IMC_Q, once L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f) is identified with L_f for the canonical periods (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/fw-ordinary-selmer-form for the integral identification).
hypotheses: ordinary at p, p ∤ N, p odd
(ω, γ) good for the dual lattice in Kato's sense (17.5), so Kato's p-adic L-function is integral
at the height-one prime (ϖ): Kato's (12.5.2) or the rank-one unipotent substitute of Skinner §2.5 and Fouquet–Wan Lemma 3.13
Euler and Tamagawa corrections: the sequence uses j_* conditions away from p and the Coleman image at p; no correction is discarded

For the conclusion involving canonical L_f integrally, separately assume the O-unit period comparison of L1/fw-ordinary-selmer-form. The exact-sequence length identity itself uses Kato’s specified analytic term.
proofSteps: Take the limit of the Poitou–Tate sequences for T(r) over Q(ζ_{p^n}) (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/selmer-structure-poitou-tate, SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-selmer-duality) to get Kato (17.13.1).

Show lim H¹_c of the strict condition vanishes (17.13.2) because the image of Z already has Λ-rank one, identify the local quotient with the Coleman map image (17.9; PadicHodgeRegulators:L3/rubin-coleman-map) and use finiteness of H²_loc (17.13.4).
Kato's explicit reciprocity (KatoEulerSystems:L3/generalised-explicit-reciprocity-law-for-zeta-elements) identifies the Coleman image of z with L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f).
Compare lengths at each height-one prime; both directions of the equivalence follow from the additivity of length in the four-term sequence.
acceptance: Kato 17.13 derives Theorem 17.4(2)–(3) from Theorem 12.5 by this sequence, and remarks (p.274) that Conjecture 12.10 implies the ordinary main conjecture 17.6; the length identity gives the converse as well.
Fouquet–Wan Lemma 4.50 is the analogous equivalence with the signed or v^∨-Selmer group in place of X.

nodes.title: Signed Selmer groups from Coleman maps
nodes.statement: Let D be a datum with p ∤ N whose local representation at p is crystalline, and fix a good basis ν₁, ν₂ of D_cris and its lift n₁, n₂ to the Wach module (LLZ §3.3, Lemma 3.15), giving Coleman maps Col_i : H¹_Iw(Q_p, T_K) → Λ_E(G_∞), i = 1, 2 (PadicHodgeRegulators:L4/signed-local-condition). For n ≥ 0 let H¹_f(Q_{p,n}, A^*)_i be the orthogonal complement, under the local Tate pairing between H¹(Q_{p,n}, T_K) and H¹(Q_{p,n}, A^*), of the image of ker(Col_i) in H¹(Q_{p,n}, T_K); here A^* is the discrete module paired with T_K in LLZ's Definition 6.4. The i-th signed Selmer group is Sel^i(Q(μ_{p^∞}), A^*) := lim_n ker(Sel(Q(μ_{p^n}), A^*) → H¹(Q_{p,n}, A^*)/H¹_f(Q_{p,n}, A^*)_i), with Bloch–Kato conditions away from p, and X^i := its Pontryagin dual, a finitely generated Λ(G_∞)-module.
hypotheses: p ∤ N, V_f|G_{Q_p} crystalline with the Wach-module basis fixed; the groups depend on that basis
for supersingular f LLZ's assumption (A) (k ≥ 3 or a_p = 0) and for good ordinary f assumption (A') (k ≥ 3 and V_f not locally split) are needed for cotorsion, not for the definition
proofSteps: The local condition on H¹_Iw(Q_p, T_K) is PadicHodgeRegulators:L4/signed-local-condition (the kernel of Col_j for the chosen good Wach basis, PadicHodgeRegulators:L4/good-wach-basis); its orthogonal complement at each finite layer is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L1/orthogonal-complement.

Glue with the Bloch–Kato conditions away from p (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/selmer-data) and take the direct limit; finite generation of the dual as for ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-dual.
The Poitou–Tate sequence H¹(T_K) → Im(Col_i) → X^i → H²(T_K) → 0 (LLZ (60)) records how X^i sits between Kato's modules.
acceptance: For a change b′ = b B of the actual good Λ-basis of (φ*N(T))^(ψ=0), the coordinate column changes by B⁻¹. A Wach-module change U first induces a change through φ and the Mellin comparison; its matrix must not be substituted for B without proof.
For a_p = 0 and the basis of LLZ Proposition 5.10, X^1 and X^2 are Kobayashi's minus and plus Selmer duals (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L4/kobayashi-pollack-comparison).

nodes.title: The signed main conjecture with the Coleman-image term
nodes.statement: For the data of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/signed-selmer-dual, put L̃_{p,i} := Col_i(loc_p z_Kato) ∈ Λ_E(G_∞). The i-th signed main conjecture SMC^{i,η} is the proposition: X^{i,η} is Λ-torsion and char_Λ(X^{i,η}) = char_Λ(Im(Col_i)^η / Λ·L̃^η_{p,i}). Only when Im(Col_i)^η is computed to be Λ (or Λ_E rationally) does it simplify to char(X^{i,η}) = (L̃^η_{p,i}).
hypotheses: the Coleman-image correction is part of the statement; replacing it by the principal ideal (L̃_{p,i}) is a separate theorem (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L4/llz-basis-adjusted-simplification)
L̃_{p,i} depends on the Wach basis; it is related to the unbounded refined functions L̃_{p,α}, L̃_{p,β} by the logarithm matrix M of LLZ Theorem 3.25 (PadicHodgeRegulators:L4/logarithmic-matrix)

Fix the integral Coleman domain and its actual finitely generated Λ-lattice I_i = Im Col_i inside Λ_E. For an integral statement require Z(f,T_K) ⊂ H¹(T_K), L̃_{p,i} ∈ I_i and L̃_{p,i}^η ≠ 0. The quotient I_i^η/Λ L̃^η is then a finitely generated torsion Λ-module even if I_i is fractional.
proofSteps: Form X^{i,η} and the Λ-submodule Im(Col_i)^η ⊂ Λ_E(G_∞)^η; the quotient by L̃^η_{p,i} is torsion when L̃^η_{p,i} ≠ 0 (LLZ Corollary 3.29, Proposition 3.39).

Take char_Λ of the actual fractional-lattice quotient, retaining its integral Λ-module structure. LLZ Remark 6.7 does not force inversion of p: a fractional embedding of a finitely generated lattice does not change its coefficient ring. The rational version separately tensors both modules with E.
acceptance: If Im(Col_i)^η = Λ, the proposition reads char(X^{i,η}) = (L̃^η_{p,i}).

At a_p = 0 and weight two, the LLZ maps have the Kobayashi kernels (1 = minus, 2 = plus). Translating analytic ideals uses the explicit Coleman images and period scalars. Proposition 5.10/Corollary 5.11 give rational unit comparisons; an integral equality of Pollack ideals also requires an integral unit normalization.

nodes.title: The signed reformulation of Kato's main conjecture
nodes.statement: Assume LLZ's (A) if f is supersingular at p, or (A') if f is good ordinary, and (E): some basis of T_f has image of Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_{p^∞})) containing SL₂(Z_p). Then for each η ∈ Δ^∨ (with i = 1 for every η and i = 2 for η trivial): X^{i,η} is Λ-torsion, there is an exact sequence 0 → (H¹/Z)^η → (Im(Col_i)/L̃_{p,i})^η → X^{i,η} → H²^η → 0, and KMC^η(T_K) ⟺ SMC^{i,η}. Without (E) the same holds rationally, and the divisibility ϖ^{n_i}L̃^η_{p,i} ∈ char(X^{i,η}) holds for some n_i ≥ 0.

As in Kobayashi Theorem 7.3, the first map of (60) is injective, giving (61); taking characteristic ideals in the four-term sequence gives the equivalence (LLZ Corollary 6.6).
Kato's divisibility Theorem 6.1(d)–(e) (KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction) gives the divisibility in Theorem 6.5.

nodes.title: Residual hypotheses of the main theorems
nodes.statement: For a two-dimensional representation ρ̄ : G_Q → GL_F(W) over a finite field F of characteristic p > 2, with decomposition and inertia groups D_ℓ ⊃ I_ℓ at each prime ℓ, define the following predicates. (irred): W has no G_Q-stable line. (dist) at p: ρ̄|D_p has a D_p-stable line on which D_p acts by χ̄₁ with quotient χ̄₂ and χ̄₁ ≠ χ̄₂. (SU_q): q ≠ p, q ∥ N and ρ̄(I_q) ≠ 1. (FW1.6_ℓ), in Fouquet–Wan's cohomological normalisation (det ρ̄ = χ̄_cyc^{1−k}): ℓ ≠ p, ℓ ∥ N, dim_F W^{I_ℓ} = 1 and dim_F W^{D_ℓ} = 0. (FWexp_ℓ(μ)): ℓ ≠ p and ρ̄|D_ℓ is a nonsplit extension 0 → μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} → ρ̄|D_ℓ → μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} → 0 with μ unramified quadratic or trivial and ρ̄(I_ℓ) ≠ 1. (LocExc_p): there is no character χ̄ of D_p with (ρ̄|D_p)^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc. (ScalarExc_p): there is no χ̄ with (ρ̄|D_p)^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄. (Im): there is σ ∈ G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} with T/(σ − 1)T free of rank one over O, for a lattice T lifting ρ̄. These predicates are evaluated on the chosen residual representation. Residual semisimplification is lattice-independent; extension and ramification data need not be. Under residual irreducibility all stable lattices are homothetic, so their residual representations agree up to isomorphism. (Im) is an integral condition on T.
hypotheses: p odd
the normalisation of ρ̄ matters for (FW1.6_ℓ): in the homological normalisation (det = χ̄_cyc^{k−1}) the inertia-invariant line carries a different character
k is the weight of the form under consideration; (FWexp_ℓ) uses k even, automatic for trivial nebentypus
proofSteps: Each predicate is a finite-dimensional linear-algebra condition on the restriction of ρ̄ to D_ℓ, I_ℓ or G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})}; use Mathlib's Representation.invariants for the invariant subspaces.

At a Steinberg prime ℓ ≠ p, inertia acts unipotently. For an elliptic curve, after the unramified quadratic extension in the nonsplit case, its residual inertia action is nontrivial iff p ∤ ord_ℓ(q_E) = ord_ℓ(Δ_min). This is an inertia criterion: divisibility of the valuation does not assert that q_E is a p-th power in Q_ℓ itself, where a unit obstruction can remain.
acceptance: Weight two, cohomological normalisation, ℓ ∥ N_E multiplicative, ρ̄ ramified at ℓ: (FW1.6_ℓ) ⟺ E has nonsplit multiplicative reduction at ℓ ⟺ (FWexp_ℓ(μ)) with μ nontrivial; for k > 2 the dimension condition (FW1.6_ℓ) means μ(ℓ)ℓ^{1−k/2} ≢ 1 mod ϖ, which is neither implied by nor implies μ nontrivial.
(SU_q) ⟸ (FW1.6_q): the second is strictly stronger; E = 11a1 at p = 7 satisfies (SU_11) but not (FW1.6_11), since 11a1 is split at 11.

nodes.title: A ramified multiplicative prime gives a rank-one quotient
nodes.statement: Let T be a free O-module of rank two with a continuous G_Q-action ρ, and q ≠ p a prime at which ρ restricted to I_q is unipotent and nontrivial modulo ϖ (as for a newform with q ∥ N, trivial character, and ρ̄ ramified at q). For τ ∈ I_q mapping to a topological generator of the tame quotient, ρ(τ) is unipotent, ρ̄(τ) ≠ 1, T/(ρ(τ) − 1)T is free of rank one over O, and τ ∈ G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})}. More generally, any σ with ρ(σ) unipotent and ρ̄(σ) ≠ 1 has T/(ρ(σ) − 1)T ≅ O.
hypotheses: q ∥ N with π(f)_q an unramified twist of Steinberg, so that inertia acts unipotently on V_f (local–global compatibility)
proofSteps: Local–global compatibility at q (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4/conductor-and-local-factors-classical) makes ρ(I_q) unipotent through the tame quotient.
For a unipotent u ≠ 1 mod ϖ on O², u − 1 has rank one modulo ϖ, so its image is a saturated rank-one submodule and the cokernel is free of rank one (elementary divisors).
q is unramified in Q(μ_{p^∞}), so I_q ⊂ G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})}.
acceptance: The matrix [[1, ϖ],[0, 1]] is unipotent with cokernel O/ϖ ⊕ O of (u − 1): it is not free, which is why ρ̄(τ) ≠ 1 is needed.
Applied with q = 11 for 11a1 at p = 7, this gives (Im) for Burungale–Castella–Skinner Theorem 1.1.2(b).

Residual unipotence is insufficient even with determinant one: g = [[1,1],[ϖ,1+ϖ]] lies in SL₂(O), but det(g−1) = −ϖ ≠ 0, ker(g−1) = 0 and coker(g−1) ≅ O/ϖ. The characteristic-zero unipotence hypothesis is essential.

sources.match: a ramified q ∥ N gives a unipotent ρ_f(τ) ≠ 1 mod ϖ, so T_f/(ρ_f(τ) − 1)T_f is free of rank one, with τ ∈ G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})}; this replaces Kato's SL₂(Z_p)-image hypothesis

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban ordinary main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)) a newform with trivial character, ordinary at p with respect to L, p ∤ N, k ≡ 2 mod (p − 1), (irred) and (dist) for ρ̄, and a prime q ≠ p with q ∥ N and ρ̄ ramified at q. Then for every finite set Σ of primes not containing p, X^Σ is Λ-torsion and char_Λ(X^Σ) = (L_f^Σ) in Λ: IMC^Σ holds integrally. In weight two this is the form p ≥ 3, f ordinary, ρ̄ irreducible, q ∥ N with ρ̄ ramified at q.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; trivial character; k ≡ 2 mod p − 1 (automatic for k = 2)
(dist) is automatic in weight two for p odd, the cohomological quotient having inertia character ω⁻¹ while the sub-character is unramified
integrality: Skinner–Urban print it under an SL₂(Z_p)-image hypothesis; Skinner §2.5 shows (irred) and the ramified q suffice, via ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient
proofSteps: Reverse divisibility (L_f^Σ L_{f⊗χ_K}^Σ) ⊃ Ch^Σ(f)Ch^Σ(f⊗χ_K) for an imaginary quadratic K in which p splits, the prime divisors of N/q split and q is inert: the GU(2,2) Eisenstein congruence argument of Skinner–Urban Theorem 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.3, owned by AutomorphicCongruences:L1.

Kato's divisibilities (L_f^Σ) ⊂ Ch^Σ(f) and (L_{f⊗χ_K}^Σ) ⊂ Ch^Σ(f⊗χ_K) (KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility), made integral by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient as in Skinner §2.5.
If the first Kato inclusion were strict the product inclusion would be strict, contradicting the reverse divisibility; so (L_f^Σ) = Ch^Σ(f) (Skinner–Urban proof of Theorem 3.6.4).
Independence of Σ: ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/euler-factor-change; the statement for Σ = ∅ follows.
acceptance: E = 11a1, p = 7: k = 2, a_7 = −2 unit, (irred), q = 11 ∥ 11 with 7 ∤ ord_11(Δ) = 5, so IMC holds integrally for 11a1 at 7.

nodes.title: The Fouquet–Wan ordinary theorem
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)) an eigencuspform with p ∤ N and k ≥ 2, such that: ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible; (FW1.6_ℓ) holds for some ℓ ∥ N (in Fouquet–Wan's cohomological normalisation); and ρ_f|G_{Q_p} is an extension 0 → χ₁ → ρ_f|G_{Q_p} → χ₂ → 0 with χ̄₁ ≠ χ̄₂. Then char(H¹(Z[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)/Λ_Iw·z(f)_Iw) divides char(H²(Z[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)), and together with Kato's divisibility this gives KMC^{η=1} over Q_∞ (Fouquet–Wan Conjecture 1.5) integrally.
hypotheses: p > 2, p ∤ N, trivial character, k ≥ 2 (no congruence condition on k)
(FW1.6_ℓ) in cohomological normalisation; in weight two it means nonsplit multiplicative reduction at ℓ with ρ̄ ramified there
the ordinary filtration with distinct residual characters
proofSteps: Kato's divisibility in this range: Fouquet–Wan Lemma 3.13 verifies its hypotheses (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/zeta-basis-characteristic-equivalence; KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction).

Reverse divisibility: Fouquet–Wan §4.8 — choose the auxiliary imaginary quadratic K as in §4.6, prove the two-variable Rankin–Selberg Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture over K by reducing it, through Beilinson–Flach explicit reciprocity and Poitou–Tate, to the GU(3,1) divisibility Theorem 7.32, in weight k (Castella–Wan Theorem 3.8 in weight two); then descend with Kato's result. The whole reverse-divisibility route is owned by AutomorphicCongruences:L2 (RS-11 owner record), which also needs KatoEulerSystems:L4 for its twist/factor separation.
Combine the two divisibilities at every height-one prime (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/kato-main-conjecture, KMC.iff_reverse_divisibility).
No canonical-versus-Gross period comparison is used: §4.8 bypasses it, and the plan records that comparison as absent rather than assumed.
acceptance: E = 14a1, p = 13, ℓ = 2: hypotheses hold (nonsplit at 2, 13 ∤ 6, χ̄₁ unramified ≠ χ̄₂ with inertia character ω⁻¹), so KMC holds for 14a1 at 13.
E = 11a1, p = 7: (FW1.6_11) fails, so this theorem does not apply even though ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/su-ordinary-theorem does.

nodes.title: The ordinary Selmer form of the ordinary theorems
nodes.statement: Assume the hypotheses of L1/fw-ordinary-theorem and, in addition, a proved identity L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f) = u L_f with u ∈ O^× for Kato’s good pair for the dual lattice and Skinner–Urban’s canonical periods. Then IMC(D) holds integrally. Conversely, under L1/su-ordinary-theorem and this same integral period identification, KMC^{η=1}(T_K) follows from IMC. The rational comparison only needs the nonzero period scalar carried into the analytic object. The unit identification in general weight is an explicit input, not a conclusion of the rational Deligne-period quotient.
hypotheses: ordinary, p ∤ N, p odd, trivial character
(irred), and a rank-one unipotent element (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient) to work at the prime (ϖ)
Kato's good pair (ω, γ) for the dual lattice U ≅ T*(1−k) (KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility, hypothesis (3))

Integral period compatibility: the Kato good dual pair and the canonical modular-symbol periods produce a scalar in O^×. A saturated rank-one lattice in each realization alone does not prove this comparison.
proofSteps: Apply ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-cohomological-comparison at every height-one prime, including (ϖ) by the rank-one quotient.

Apply Kato’s explicit reciprocity with its actual period scalar. If the integral period-compatibility input gives a unit, the analytic ideals agree. KatoEulerSystems:L3/archimedean-period-quotient-and-critical-values supplies an algebraic period quotient, not by itself its O-unit valuation.
Translate Fouquet–Wan's T and Λ_Iw into the datum D by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-convention-dictionary.

General-weight translation retains the period-compatibility input.
A period choice not saturated in the integral lattice gives L_{p-adic} = ϖ^m u L_f with m ≠ 0, and the integral equality would fail by ϖ^m.

nodes.title: Skinner's theorem for multiplicative reduction
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) a newform with p ∥ N (so f is ordinary at p, k = 2, and a_p = ±1), L/Q_p as in the datum, (irred) for ρ̄_f, and a prime q ≠ p with q ∥ N and ρ̄_f ramified at q. Then for every finite Σ not containing p, X^Σ is Λ-torsion and char_Λ(X^Σ) = (L_f^Σ) in Λ, where X^Σ uses the ordinary line of the Steinberg representation at p and L_f is the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum p-adic L-function (with its trivial zero when a_p = 1).
hypotheses: p ≥ 3, p ∥ N, weight two, trivial character
(irred) and a ramified q ∥ N, q ≠ p

the p ∤ N seed is ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/su-ordinary-theorem in weights k_m ≡ 2 mod (p − 1)p^m on level N/p; it is applied only to members of the Hida family satisfying its hypotheses, which the congruence modulo p guarantees

the imported Hida-family node OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.6/ordinary-newform-lies-in-a-hida-family is stated for p ≥ 5; the case p = 3 needs the same Hida-theoretic input for p = 3 (recorded as remaining work of L1)
proofSteps: Reductions: it suffices to prove the statement after a finite extension of L (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/coefficient-extension-invariance) and for Σ containing all primes dividing N (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/euler-factor-change).

Hida theory: f is the weight-two member of a Hida family (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.6/ordinary-newform-lies-in-a-hida-family); for each m > 0 there is a newform f_m ∈ S_{k_m}(Γ_0(N/p)) with k_m ≡ 2 mod (p − 1)p^m, ordinary, whose p-stabilisation is congruent to f modulo p^m.

The two-variable p-adic L-function of PadicFamilies:L1/branch-l-functions yields congruence of the principal ideals (L^Σ_{f_m}, p^m) = (L^Σ_f, p^m), with compatible choices of periods or their unit ambiguity. An exact equality of chosen analytic generators modulo p^m is not asserted without fixing these choices.

Greenberg's theorem (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-structure) gives Ch^Σ(f_m) = Fitt(X^Σ(f_m)); the congruence gives Sel^Σ(f)[p^m] ≅ Sel^Σ(f_m)[p^m], hence (Fitt(X^Σ(f)), p^m) = (Ch^Σ(f_m), p^m) = (L^Σ_{f_m}, p^m) = (L^Σ_f, p^m) for every m.
Since L^Σ_f ≠ 0, Fitt(X^Σ(f)) ≠ 0, so X^Σ(f) is torsion, Greenberg's theorem gives Ch^Σ(f) = Fitt, and principal ideals agreeing modulo every p^m are equal.
acceptance: For E with split multiplicative reduction at p, L_f has a trivial zero at the trivial character and the theorem is consistent with Greenberg–Stevens (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/greenberg-stevens-trivial-zero): (γ − 1) divides both sides.
The theorem is the input requested by RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6/rank-zero-ordinary-multiplicative-p-part for p ∥ N (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/4(a)).

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan conventions against the modular Iwasawa datum
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)) with trivial character. Fouquet–Wan's T(f) ⊂ M(f)_{et,p} is a lattice in the cohomological realisation, with det ρ_f = χ_cyc^{1−k}, and their Λ_Iw-adic objects are RΓ_et(Z[1/p], T(f) ⊗ Λ_Iw), Δ(M(f))_Iw and the {p}-partial zeta morphism z(f)_Iw : T(f)_Iw(−1)^+ → H¹(Z[1/p], T(f)_Iw). Under the dictionary T(f) ↔ Kato's T_K (KatoEulerSystems:L2/hecke-dual-twist-dictionary) and Λ_Iw ↔ the η = 1 quotient Λ of Λ(G_∞), these are the objects H^i(T_K), Δ_Iw(T_K) and triv_z of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/iwasawa-fundamental-line, and Fouquet–Wan's Conjecture 1.5 for M(f) is KMC^{η=1}(T_K). The half-weight twists χ_cyc^{1−k/2}, χ_cyc^{−k/2} in Fouquet–Wan's local hypothesis are integral powers because k is even for trivial character. More precisely z(f)_Iw = (∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖{p}} Eul_ℓ(V_f^*(1)))⁻¹ z(f)_Σ,Iw in the total fraction algebra (Proposition 3.28, p.35); the local determinant corrections must accompany this formula integrally.

the dictionary of Hecke actions and twists is the one fixed in KatoEulerSystems:L2/hecke-dual-twist-dictionary; no other convention is introduced here

nodes.title: The Fouquet–Wan pointwise main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, F a finite field of characteristic p and ρ̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F) absolutely irreducible and odd, satisfying: (LocExc_p); and for some ℓ ≠ p, (FWexp_ℓ(μ)) — a ramified extension 0 → μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} → ρ̄|D_ℓ → μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} → 0 with μ unramified quadratic (possibly trivial), and μ nontrivial if ρ̄|G_{Q_p} is irreducible. Let f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(Np^r)) be a normalised eigencuspform of weight k ≥ 2 with ρ̄_f ≅ ρ̄ and ℓ ∥ N. Then KMC^{η=1} holds for f integrally: the zeta morphism induces Δ_{O_Iw}(T(f)_Iw) ≅ O_Iw (Fouquet–Wan Conjecture 3.24 = 1.5). In particular this holds for every reduction type of f at p (crystalline, semistable, potentially semistable; principal series, Steinberg or supercuspidal π(f)_p).
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; k ≥ 2 is even and the nebentypus is trivial. Theorem 5.1 permits level Np^r; μ is an unramified quadratic character, allowed to be trivial when the local representation at p is reducible.

The scalar semisimplification is automatically excluded: det ρ̄_f = χ̄_cyc^(1−k) has odd exponent, whereas a scalar semisimplification has square determinant on tame inertia (Fouquet–Wan remark following Theorem 5.1, p.69).
Assumption 2.1(1), absolute irreducibility over Q(√p*), follows from the genuine ramified unipotent at ℓ; Assumption 3.5 follows from (LocExc_p).
proofSteps: The proof is owned by AutomorphicCongruences:L4 (RS-11 narrowing): the universal-family theorem (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L4/fw-universal-family-theorem) at points of X^sm via ordinary/crystalline-short points and the GU(3,1) congruence, propagated to all classical points by the height-one descent of Fouquet–Wan §§5–6.

This node states the endpoint in the datum's conventions: translate by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-convention-dictionary, and check the residual hypotheses with ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/residual-hypothesis-predicates.
Derive Assumption 2.1(1) from the ramified unipotent at ℓ (the image of G_{Q(√p*)} contains ρ̄(I_ℓ), and an induced-from-quadratic image has no nontrivial unipotent elements for p odd).
acceptance: E = 14a1, p = 5 (supersingular, a_5 = 0): ρ̄|G_{Q_5} is irreducible, so (LocExc_5), (ScalarExc_5) hold; ℓ = 2 is nonsplit (μ nontrivial) and 5 ∤ ord_2 Δ = 6, so ρ̄ is ramified at 2; ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible (no rational 5-isogeny). KMC holds for 14a1 at p = 5.

E = 11a1, p = 7: ρ̄|G_{Q_7} is reducible (ordinary), so Theorem 5.1 allows μ trivial at ℓ = 11 (split); with 7 ∤ 5 and ā_7² = 4 ≠ 1 the hypotheses hold, while the introduction's Theorem 1.7 (μ nontrivial) does not apply.

nodes.title: Elliptic curves against their newforms: lattices and periods
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have conductor N and newform f_E (EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6/modularity-theorem), and fix the modular parametrisation φ_E : X_0(N) → E of EllipticCurveModularity:R29.5/modular-parametrisation through a Q-isogeny λ : A_{f_E} → E, with φ_E^*ω_E = c_φ·2πi f_E(z)dz. Then: (1) T_pE ≅ T for the datum of f_E with Tate lattice λ_*⁻¹(T_pE) in V_p(A_{f_E}) and the corresponding cohomological dual lattice T_f; (2) write Ω_E^± for the periods of a Néron differential ω_E and Ω_{f_E}^± for the canonical periods defined by the saturated f_E-isotypic part of H¹(X_0(N), Z_{(p)})^±; for the X_0(N)-optimal curve φ_{E,*} is surjective on integral homology, so φ_E^* identifies H¹(E(C), Z_{(p)})^± with that saturated part and Ω_E^± = ±c_φ·u^±·P_{f_E}^±, where P_{f_E}^± := −2πi Ω_{f_E}^± in Skinner–Urban’s cohomological convention with u^± ∈ Z_{(p)}^×; for a curve E' isogenous to the optimal curve the ratio is multiplied by the period ratio of the isogeny, a rational number whose p-part divides a power of the p-part of the isogeny degree; (3) for p > 2 semistable for E and φ_E optimal, p ∤ c_φ (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.3/manin-integrality-and-p-unit). Every nonunit factor is retained; none is assumed to be 1.

p > 3, so that H¹(X_0(N), Z_(p)) is the parabolic cohomology of Γ_0(N) with Z_(p) coefficients used to define canonical periods
the isogeny λ is part of the data; for the X_0(N)-optimal curve λ = id
(3) needs p > 2 semistable and φ_E optimal; otherwise c_φ is only an integer
proofSteps: Modularity and the parametrisation: EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6/modularity-theorem and R29.5/modular-parametrisation.

Use R29.4/tate-module-comparison rationally, then choose λ_*⁻¹(T_pE) in V_p(A_{f_E}) and its corresponding cohomological dual lattice. Although λ_* is a rational isomorphism, λ_*T_p(A_{f_E}) can be a proper sublattice of T_pE when p divides deg λ.

Periods: φ_E^*ω_E = c_φ·2πi f_E(z)dz; since φ_{E,*} is surjective on H_1 for the optimal curve, φ_E^* is injective on H¹ with torsion-free cokernel, so φ_E^*H¹(E(C), Z_(p))^± is a saturated rank-one sublattice of the f_E-part, hence equal to it; pairing gives the period relation. The canonical periods are those of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/integral-period-lattices. Here the differential period is P_f=−2πiΩ_f, as in Skinner 2016 footnote 6, rather than the cohomological Ω_f itself.
Manin constant: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.3/manin-integrality-and-p-unit (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/17).

For a p-isogeny, the image of the source Tate lattice can be proper in T_pE, and the Néron period ratio can be nonunit (e.g. p=5 in class 11a). Track both lattice and analytic period factors. Under residual irreducibility stable lattices are homothetic, so this issue disappears for the integral irreducible branches.

Its analytic form is L_p(E, s) = ∫ ⟨x⟩^{s−1} μ_{E,α}. If E[p] is irreducible, L_p(E/Q) ∈ Λ.

Under ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/curve-form-lattice-dictionary, MMC(E, p) ⟺ IMC(D_{f_E}) when the period ratio Ω_E^+/P_{f_E}^+ (P_f=−2πiΩ_f) is a p-adic unit, and MMC_Q(E, p) ⟺ IMC_Q(D_{f_E}) always.

nodes.title: Residual surjectivity gives the rank-one image condition
nodes.statement: Let E/Q, p ≥ 5, and suppose ρ̄_{E,p} : G_Q → GL₂(F_p) is surjective. Then the image of ρ_{E,p^∞} is GL₂(Z_p), the image of G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} contains SL₂(Z_p), and σ with ρ_{E,p^∞}(σ) = [[1, 1], [0, 1]] satisfies T_pE/(σ − 1)T_pE ≅ Z_p, so (Im) holds.
hypotheses: residual surjectivity onto GL₂(F_p)
proofSteps: Let H be the closed p-adic image. Its closed commutator subgroup lies in SL₂(Z_p) and reduces onto [GL₂(F_p),GL₂(F_p)]=SL₂(F_p). Serre’s SL₂ lifting lemma for p≥5 makes this subgroup SL₂(Z_p). Since det H is all Z_p× (Weil pairing), H=GL₂(Z_p).
Q(μ_{p^∞}) is cut out by the determinant, so G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} maps onto SL₂(Z_p) ∩ image = SL₂(Z_p).
For u = [[1,1],[0,1]], u − 1 has image Z_p·e₁, so the quotient is free of rank one (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient).
acceptance: For E = 14a1 and p = 5 (5 is not a nonmaximal prime for 14a1), ρ̄_{E,5} is surjective, so (Im) holds.
Burungale–Castella–Skinner Remark 1.1.3(i): for non-CM E, (Im) holds for all sufficiently large p by Serre's open image theorem.

Identifying this derived coefficient object with the specialized arithmetic lattice, primitive line and zeta trivialization requires Fouquet–Wan’s relative-purity and Iwasawa-suitability conditions, using Definition 3.19 for the regular base (Definition 3.12 is for the Hecke-algebra setting). At a classical point the primitive zeta map satisfies z_primitive = (∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖{p}} Eul_ℓ(V_f^*(1)))⁻¹ z_Σ (Proposition 3.28); compatible local determinant factors accompany it. These nonzero factors need not be units. Characteristic ideals are recovered from the specialized determinant with all cohomology and Tor terms, rather than specialized term by term.

nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good supersingular reduction at an odd prime p with a_p = 0. For the LLZ basis there are units a^± ∈ Λ_E(G_∞)^× with a^−·Col₁ = Col^− and a^+·Col₂ = Col^+, where Col^± are the plus and minus Coleman maps whose kernels define Kobayashi's local conditions E^±; consequently (1) the signed Selmer groups X¹, X² of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/signed-selmer-dual are Kobayashi's Sel^−(E/Q_∞)^∨ and Sel^+(E/Q_∞)^∨; (2) L̃_{p,1}, L̃_{p,2} are Pollack's L_p^−, L_p^+ up to units of Λ_E(G_∞), and the decomposition of L̃_{p,α}, L̃_{p,β} in LLZ Theorem 1.3 reduces to Pollack's decomposition with the half-logarithms log^±_p; (3) SMC^{1,η}, SMC^{2,η} are Kobayashi's minus and plus main conjectures char(Sel^∓(E/Q_∞)^{∨,η}) = char(Im(Col^∓)^η/(L_p^{∓,η})). They identify kernels integrally and carry each actual image lattice to its corresponding image lattice, hence identify the corrected image quotients when the zeta images use the same period normalization. nodes.title: Changing the imprimitive set: Euler factors on both sides
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary datum with trivial character, p ∤ N, and Σ' ⊂ Σ finite sets of primes not containing p. If X^Σ is Λ-torsion and T* has no nonzero G_Q-invariants, then 0 → (⊕_{ℓ∈Σ∖Σ'} H¹(Q_{∞,ℓ}, A))^∨ → X^Σ → X^{Σ'} → 0 is exact, each local term is torsion with no nonzero pseudo-null submodule and characteristic ideal (P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ)), where P_{T,ℓ} is the Euler polynomial of Skinner–Urban Lemma 3.2.17(ii) and γ_ℓ ∈ Γ is the image of Frob_ℓ; hence char(X^Σ) = char(X^{Σ'})·∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖Σ'} (P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ)). On the analytic side L_f^Σ = L_f^{Σ'}·∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖Σ'} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ) with the same factors. Therefore IMC^Σ(D) ⟺ IMC^{Σ'}(D), integrally and rationally, and the same holds for KMC with Σ-partial lines.
hypotheses: X^Σ torsion (it then follows for Σ')
T* has no nonzero G_Q-invariants (true when ρ̄ is irreducible)
the same polynomial P_{T,ℓ} must be used on both sides; using the Euler factor of V where that of its dual is meant breaks the equality

For the displayed exact sequence require Σ ∪ {p} to contain the ramification set, as in SU Proposition 3.2.18. Comparisons between arbitrary Σ,Σ′ pass through a common larger set containing that set; no unconditional localization-surjectivity assertion is made.
proofSteps: For a large Σ containing every ramified prime other than p, use SU Proposition 3.2.18. For arbitrary finite sets, compare each with a common larger set and cancel the identical nonzero analytic/algebraic Euler factors in the domain Λ.
Local terms: Skinner–Urban Lemma 3.2.17 — torsion, no pseudo-null submodules, characteristic ideal generated by the Euler polynomial at ℓ^{-1}ε_Q(frob_ℓ).
Analytic side: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L4/primitive-imprimitive-level-change.
Multiplicativity of characteristic ideals in exact sequences: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 (charIdeal_mul_of_exact).

Since Λ → Λ_{O'} is faithfully flat, IMC^Σ(D ⊗ O') ⟺ IMC^Σ(D), and similarly for KMC and SMC.

characteristic ideals over the regular rings Λ, Λ_{O'}

Characteristic ideals commute with flat base change between normal noetherian domains when heights are preserved (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4, base change of charIdeal).

nodes.title: μ- and λ-invariants of the two sides
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser ϖ, Λ = O[[X]], and f, g ∈ Λ nonzero. If (f)Λ[1/ϖ] = (g)Λ[1/ϖ] and ϖ^n | f ⟺ ϖ^n | g for all n (equal μ-invariants), then f and g are associated in Λ. Consequently: (1) IMC(D) implies μ(X) = μ(L_f) and λ(X) = λ(L_f); (2) IMC_Q(D) together with μ(X) = μ(L_f) implies IMC(D); (3) the same holds for KMC and Mazur's conjecture; in particular IMC_Q(D) and μ(L_f) = 0 = μ(X) give the integral conjecture.
hypotheses: O a complete DVR; Λ = O[[X]] a UFD
μ and λ invariants of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 §4.4
proofSteps: Λ is a UFD with ϖ prime; the units of Λ[1/ϖ] are ϖ^Z·Λ^×; so (f) = (g) in Λ[1/ϖ] means f = ϖ^m u g with m ∈ Z, u ∈ Λ^×, and equal μ forces m = 0.
For (1): Weierstrass preparation f = ϖ^μ P u (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 §4.3–4.4) and char(X) = (ϖ^{μ(X)} char-poly) give equality of invariants.
Apply to f = a generator of char(X), g = L_f.
acceptance: μ(X) = μ(L_f) = 0 and IMC_Q imply IMC: this is how integral statements are obtained once μ-vanishing is known.
f = p, g = 1 have (f) = (g) in Λ[1/p] but different μ, so the μ-hypothesis is necessary.

nodes.title: The rank-zero p-converse
nodes.statement: (1) (Skinner–Urban) Let E/Q, p≥3 a prime of good ordinary reduction with ρ̄_{E,p} irreducible and a prime q ≠ p, q ∥ N_E, at which ρ̄_{E,p} is ramified. If Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q) is finite then L(E,1) ≠ 0; equivalently, L(E,1) = 0 implies corank_{Z_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q) ≥ 1. The same holds at p of multiplicative reduction under Skinner's Theorem C hypotheses. (2) (Fouquet–Wan) For f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)) satisfying the hypotheses of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-pointwise-theorem with p ∤ N, the discrete Bloch–Kato Selmer group associated with a lattice in V = M(f)_{et,p}(k/2) and A=V/T is finite iff L(f, k/2) ≠ 0. (3) For f = f_E with E/Q and N not squarefull (Skinner–Urban) or arbitrary N (Wan), if rank E(Q) = 0 and Sha(E/Q)[p^∞] is finite for one sufficiently large ordinary p, then ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 0.
hypotheses: (1): the hypotheses of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/su-ordinary-theorem in weight two (or ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/skinner-multiplicative-theorem)
(2): the pointwise theorem's hypotheses
(3): the range quoted by Skinner 2020 §1; the all-N case rests on Wan's thesis, cited there

In (2) finiteness concerns the discrete p-primary Selmer group. For the Q_p-vector-space Bloch–Kato group the corresponding conclusion is zero, not finiteness of a nonzero vector space. The statement for arbitrary N in (3) is source-reported context only; no proof from the narrower ordinary theorem is asserted.
proofSteps: (1): from IMC, (γ − 1) | char(X) iff the trivial-character value vanishes; Greenberg's control (RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6/cyclotomic-specialization-formula; Skinner–Urban's proof via Greenberg [Gr99] Theorem 4.1) relates X_Γ to Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q), so L(E,1) = 0 forces positive corank.
(2): Fouquet–Wan Corollary 5.3 — if the specialisation of z(f)_Iw at γ ↦ 1 vanishes, (γ − 1) divides char(H¹/z) = char(H²), giving positive corank; otherwise its image spans a nonzero line in H¹_f.
(3): Skinner 2020 §1 records this converse from the ordinary main conjecture.
acceptance: E = 11a1 at p = 7: L(E,1) ≠ 0 and Sel_{7^∞}(E/Q) is finite, consistent with (1).
(1) is the input routed from PAPER-SKINNER-20/3; the rank-one converse is RankOneConverse:PC.3/theorem-b, not this node.

The ℒ-invariant is ℒ_p(E) := log_p(q_E)/ord_p(q_E), where log_p is Iwasawa's branch of the p-adic logarithm (log_p(p) = 0). For a weight-two newform f with p ∥ N and a_p = 1 attached to E, ℒ(V_f) := ℒ_p(E) is the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum ℒ-invariant.

nodes.title: The Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum p-adic BSD conjecture
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at an odd p, r = rank E(Q), α the unit root, L_{p,α}(E, s) the function of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/msd-padic-l-function, ⟨ , ⟩_{p,α} the p-adic height on Q_p ⊗ E(Q) attached to the splitting of the Hodge filtration given by the α-eigenline of Frobenius, and R_{p,α}(E) its regulator. MTT(E, p) is the proposition: (i) if α ≠ 1, ord_{s=1} L_{p,α}(E, s) ≥ r and lim_{s→1} (s − 1)^{−r} L_{p,α}(E, s) = (1 − α^{-1})^{b+1}·#Sha(E)·R_{p,α}(E)·∏_v m_v; (ii) if α = 1, the order is ≥ r + 1 and lim_{s→1} (s − 1)^{−r−1} L_{p,α}(E, s) = ℒ_p(E)·#Sha(E)·R_{p,α}(E)·∏_v m_v. Here, as in Colmez Conjecture 0.12, R_{p,α}(E) := e^{−2} det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩_{p,α}) for P_1, …, P_r spanning Q ⊗ E(Q) and generating a subgroup of index e in E(Q) (so R_{p,α}(E) = #E(Q)_tors^{−2} when r = 0), m_v is the number of components at v (m_∞ for E(R), the Tamagawa number at finite v), and Ω_E^+ satisfies m_∞Ω_E^+ = |∫_{E(R)} ω_E|. The exact proposition MTT includes finiteness of the full Sha(E/Q), so #Sha has its usual finite meaning. Define separately MTT_p: assume only Sha(E/Q)[p∞] finite and use its order in the displayed leading-term formula up to a Z_p-unit (ratio in Z_p×), retaining the same order lower bound. If the regulator is nonzero this formula gives the exact order. These exact and unit propositions are not identified.
hypotheses: good ordinary or multiplicative p, p odd
the p-adic height pairing is an input (the Mazur–Tate/Schneider height for ordinary E); its nondegeneracy is not known in general
the torsion enters through the index e in the regulator, as in Colmez's normalisation of R_∞(E); the formula must not divide by #E(Q)_tors² a second time
MTT uses full Sha finiteness; MTT_p uses only finiteness of its p-primary part. This finiteness is supplied as an input, not inferred merely by writing #Sha.
proofSteps: State with L_{p,α}(E, s) (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/msd-padic-l-function), ℒ_p(E) (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/tate-l-invariant) and the p-adic height.

The p-adic height pairing and regulator are an input with no planned owner in the atlas (gap: the SelmerIwasawaCohomology Part II on p-adic heights is not yet a roadmap; NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.7/height-pairing-bockstein plans Nekovář's height only as a Bockstein map).
acceptance: Kato's theorem (Colmez Theorem 0.15): ord_{s=1} L_{p,α}(E,s) ≥ r (≥ r + 1 if α = 1), and equality implies Sha[p^∞] finite and R_{p,α}(E) ≠ 0 — a consequence, not an assumption.

In rank zero with α≠1 and full Sha finite, exact MTT is equivalent to the full numerical BSD formula. With only Sha[p∞] finite, MTT_p is equivalent to its p-part. Even at an anomalous ordinary prime, the nonzero factor 1−α⁻¹ cancels in the comparison; it need not be a p-adic unit.

nodes.title: Trivial zeros in analytic rank zero
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at an odd prime p with L(E,1) ≠ 0. Then ord_{s=1} L_{p,α}(E, s) ∈ {0, 1}, with order one iff E has split multiplicative reduction at p (α = 1), and in that case L'_{p,α}(E, 1) = ℒ_p(E)·L(E,1)/Ω_E^+ (Greenberg–Stevens) with ℒ_p(E) ≠ 0. Consequently, if Sha(E/Q) is finite, exact MTT(E,p) and the full classical BSD formula are equivalent; with only Sha[p∞] finite, MTT_p and the p-part are equivalent in this case.

nodes.title: The main conjecture implies p-adic BSD under nondegenerate heights
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good ordinary reduction at an odd prime p, irreducible E[p], finite Sha(E/Q)[p^∞], and a nondegenerate cyclotomic p-adic height. Use the analytic κ-height of Schneider §7, with its comparison to the height and cyclotomic coordinate in MTT_p(E,p) fixed. Assume also the flat Néron-model/Galois ordinary Selmer comparison specified below. If MMC(E,p) holds, then ord_{s=1} L_p(E,s)=rank E(Q)=r and its leading coefficient satisfies MTT_p(E,p): L_p^{(r)}(E,1)/r! ∼_p (1−α⁻¹)^2 R_p(E) · #Sha(E/Q)[p^∞] · ∏_{ℓ|N}c_ℓ(E) / #E(Q)_tors^2. Here ∼_p denotes equality up to Z_p×. This is the p-primary, up-to-unit consequence; it is not an exact MTT identity. In this display R_p is the unnormalized determinant on a basis of the free Mordell–Weil group; thus R_{p,α} of the MTT node equals R_p/#E(Q)_tors². The torsion denominator is included exactly once.
hypotheses: good ordinary p, ρ̄ irreducible
Sha[p^∞] finite and ⟨ , ⟩_{p,α} nondegenerate (both are hypotheses)
MMC(E, p) (for instance from ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/bcs-integral-theorem)
The ordinary Galois Selmer characteristic series is identified with Schneider’s algebraic Iwasawa L-function using the control/comparison request to SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3.
The height is Schneider’s analytic κ-height, or a height equipped with a proved normalization comparison. Keep log_p κ(γ)^r when passing from X to s; that factor is not a p-adic unit.
proofSteps: Apply Schneider §2 Theorem 2′ (p.342) and §7 Theorems 6–7 (p.371): the algebraic Iwasawa L-function has order r and leading coefficient, up to a p-adic unit, det(height)·#Sha[p∞]·∏_v#π_v(E)·#Ẽ(F_p)^2/#E(Q)_tors^2. Theorem 6 identifies the algebraic and analytic κ-heights up to sign.

Compare Schneider’s flat Néron-model cohomology and its alternating characteristic factors (§§1–2) with the ordinary Galois Selmer dual. Irreducibility removes global p-power torsion terms. This is the explicit supplier obligation below, rather than an assertion that the objects are definitionally equal.
Use #Ẽ(F_p)=(1−α)(1−p/α), so #Ẽ(F_p)^2 ∼_p (1−α⁻¹)^2, including anomalous primes. Transfer the characteristic-series leading term through MMC(E,p).

Schneider evaluates in the coordinate κ(γ)^{1−s}−1; the convention here uses κ(γ)^{s−1}−1. The sign contributes a unit, while the factor log_p κ(γ)^r must be matched with the regulator normalization. Use the specified height comparison to obtain the displayed MTT_p formula.

nodes.title: The modular instances of the Greenberg and Coates–Perrin-Riou propositions
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary datum with trivial character and V := V_f ⊗ det ρ_f^{-1}. (1) V is p-ordinary with Greenberg filtration F^+V = V^+ ⊗ det ρ_f^{-1}, r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0 is the criticality of the relevant twists (V^∨=Hom(V,Q_p(1)) is the Tate dual), and the trivial tame-component projection of Greenberg’s proposition (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/greenberg-main-conjecture) for (V,L_p(V)) is IMC_Q(D), after descending its Selmer group over F∞^+=Q(μ_{p∞})^+ to Q∞ and identifying that projected analytic function with L_f. (2) The Coates–Perrin-Riou existence proposition for V (owned by AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5) is satisfied by L_f: its interpolation formula at the critical twists is the Skinner–Urban formula of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/canonical-ordinary-padic-l-function with Deligne periods Ω_f^± and the modified Euler factors at p. (3) The proposition 'Greenberg's conjecture for every ordinary V' is not proved here; nor is Greenberg's μ = λ = 0 conjecture for totally real fields.
hypotheses: ordinary datum; the Coates–Perrin-Riou proposition in the form fixed by AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5

Use the trivial character of Gal(F∞^+/Q∞), whose order (p−1)/2 is a p-adic unit; the full Greenberg proposition over F∞^+ includes other tame components. V^∨ means the Tate dual, not the untwisted linear dual.
proofSteps: (1): unwind the Greenberg Selmer group of V over the cyclotomic Z_p-extension (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/greenberg-condition) as the Skinner–Urban Selmer group. sourceIssues.printed: Theorems 1.7 and 5.1 list as local hypothesis at p only that the semisimplification of ρ̄|G_{Q_p} is not of the form χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc; Theorem 1.1 also excludes χ̄ ⊕ χ̄, and the standing Assumption 2.1(2) of §2 excludes extensions with χ₁^{-1}χ₂ = 1.
sourceIssues.correction: State Theorems 1.7 and 5.1 with the additional exclusion (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄, or supply an argument for the scalar case.
sourceIssues.reason: The proofs run through §2–§4, which assume Assumption 2.1 throughout (representability and scalar endomorphisms of ρ̄|G_{Q_p}, Lemma 3.13's vanishing of H⁰); the theorems' hypotheses (2)–(3) imply Assumption 2.1(1) and Assumption 3.5 but not the scalar part of 2.1(2).
searched: arXiv versions v1–v3 abstract pages and the v3 text, read 18 October 2026; no erratum found by a bounded web search the same day; no claim of exhaustive novelty.

review.reason: The remark immediately after Theorem 5.1 (v3, p.69) explicitly explains the omission: trivial nebentypus and even weight give det ρ̄ = χ̄_cyc^(1−k), an odd power. A scalar local semisimplification would have square determinant on tame inertia; the odd exponent is not a square character since p−1 is even. No extra scalar hypothesis or gap is needed.

sourceIssues.printed: Assumption 3 (ℓ ∥ N, dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1, dim ρ̄^{G_{Q_ℓ}} = 0) is said to be equivalent to π(f)_ℓ being Steinberg twisted by the unramified character sending ℓ to −ℓ^{k/2−1}, with ρ̄|G_ℓ ramified.
sourceIssues.correction: The equivalence holds in weight two. In general, with ρ̄|D_ℓ a ramified extension of μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} by μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2}, the condition dim ρ̄^{D_ℓ} = 0 means μ(ℓ)ℓ^{1−k/2} ≢ 1 mod ϖ, which neither implies nor is implied by μ(ℓ) = −1 when k > 2.
sourceIssues.reason: The inertia-invariant line is the sub-line μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} (cohomological normalisation, as in Theorem 1.7), whose arithmetic Frobenius eigenvalue is μ(ℓ)ℓ^{1−k/2}; for k = 4 and ℓ ≡ −1 mod p with μ(ℓ) = −1 the eigenvalue is 1, and with μ(ℓ) = 1, ℓ ≢ 1 mod p it is not.
searched: arXiv v3 text read 18 October 2026; the theorems themselves are stated with their own hypotheses, so only the remark is affected; bounded web search found no correction.

review.reason: In the cohomological normalization the inertia-fixed line has Frobenius μ(ℓ)ℓ^{1−k/2}, so absence of fixed vectors is the noncongruence of that eigenvalue to 1, not merely μ(ℓ)=−1. The weight-four tests in the finding distinguish them. The theorem statements retain their own hypotheses; this finding concerns the explanatory equivalence in the arXiv v3 remark only.
